correctness.rationale: An open or closed radius-one center family in a product of finite cliques has common positive center sets along a single coordinate line when the two queries differ in one coordinate, two recombinations at distance two, and none beyond distance two. Query restrictions to a line are singleton/co-singleton/full/empty, so after two positive answers the version-space online rank is at most one, forcing uniform Ldim≤3. The closed K₂□K_q case has, after a negative root answer, candidates on one row/coordinate line, forcing Ldim≤2; the open K₂□K₃ positive root fiber has cardinality only 3, also rank≤2. Explicit VC-shattered support witnesses and two depth-three ternary rook mistake trees supply lower bounds. Small-product independent concept-mask/minimax computations checked eight mixed families and confirmed the exceptional (2,3),(2,q≥4),(3,3),binary-cube cases. The uniform proof treats all finite positive d and each q_i≥2; old static VC numbers are credited, not new.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Earlier complete equal-alphabet online theorems (November 2) are strong for H(d,q) but do not include unequal factors. Adler et al. establish static VC upper bounds; VC=2 alone cannot force Ldim=2 because K₃□K₃ has VC2 and Ldim3. The negative-row version-space proof is an additional online fact.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Taking q1≠q2 makes the old H(d,q) theorems inapplicable as equal-parameter statements. Embedding into a larger equal-q Hamming graph yields Ldim≤3 but not the sharp closed rank2. The latter follows from an independent geometry-of-negative-centers argument.

value.rationale: The exact adversarial online mistake bounds for mixed-alphabet Hamming products are natural learning-theory parameters. The sharp persistent heterogeneous difference between open and closed K₂□K_q and the isolated static-adaptive gap at K₃□K₃ cannot be obtained from a static VC table; the finite all-parameter online classification has standalone mathematical value.
